articles.title: Ferrugem grava ao vivo, em show no Rio, álbum com o repertório de Alcione | G1
articles.body:
Ferrugem vai cantar músicas como 'Além da cama' (2001) na gravação do álbum 'Legado – Ferrugem canta Alcione' — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Voz do pagode do século XXI, Ferrugem vai gravar ao vivo o álbum em que aborda o repertório de Alcione , cantora projetada como sambista em 1975.

A gravação do álbum audiovisual “Legado – Ferrugem canta Alcione” está programada para a próxima quarta-feira, 28 de outubro, em show que será apresentado pelo artista carioca somente para convidados em teatro da Barra da Tijuca, bairro da zona oeste da cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ).

A gravação terá a participação da própria Alcione. Com cerca de 15 composições, o roteiro do show prevê músicas como “Além da cama” (Michael Sullivan e Carlos Colla, 2001), “Faz uma loucura por mim” (Chico Roque e Paulo Sérgio Valle, 2001) e “Você me vira a cabeça (Me tira do sério)” (Chico Roque e Paulo Sérgio Valle, 2001), entre outros sucessos da cantora.

articles.title: Travis Kelce Says Brother Jason Woke Him Up with a Phone Call That Taylor Swift Called ‘F---ed Up’
articles.summary: Jason’s early morning phone call left Travis cracking up and his wife cranky
articles.body:
During the Oct. 21 episode of 'New Heights,' Travis Kelce revealed an early morning call his brother made that left his wife, Taylor Swift, less than amused

Jason Kelce called Travis Kelce early to ask him to spot a bench press session during "Squatober"

Travis initially feared his brother had been injured after receiving the 7:30 a.m. call

If Jason Kelce isn't careful, he might end up in sister-in-law Taylor Swift 's bad books.

The 38-year-old retired NFL star and the older brother of Swift's husband, Travis Kelce , recently woke Travis and Swift up with an early morning call.

The brothers laughed off the exchange on the Wednesday, Oct. 21 episode of their New Heights podcast, where they discussed Jason participating in a challenge called "Squatober."

"I knew Jason was doing Squatober," Travis said. "He actually asked me how much weight I have in my basement. I didn't even add it up. I just told him how many weights I had. And he was like, 'Oh, okay, cool, I'll bring some.' So he flew to Kansas City with — what was it, 50 lbs.?"

Jason confirmed that he flew to Kansas City, Mo., with two 25 lb. weights to help his squat game.

"A couple extra plates to throw on the old squat bar," Travis said. "Absolutely hilarious, the most meathead thing I think I've ever seen Jason do."

But Squatober also led to an early morning call that caught Travis and his pop star wife off guard.

"I get a call at 7:30 in the morning. In my mind, I'm thinking worst-case scenario," the Kansas City Chiefs tight end explained. "I'm like, 'Oh, s---. Is everything okay? Maybe after the run Jason's in the hospital, he blew his knee out or something.' I dunno, I was worst-case scenario, the brain was just waking up. I was like, 'Uhh, you okay?' "

Not only was Jason fine, he was calling with a workout-related request.

"Jason's like, 'Yeah, can you come spot me?' I was just like, 'No way!' " Travis recalled, cracking up.

"I got my ankle wrap. And he's like, 'Nah, nah, it's bench, it's bench. It's not squat.' And I'm like, cool, 'cause I wouldn't be able to save you if it was a f---ing back squat. I'm like, 'Cool, I'll come down.' "

And while Travis was immediately game to help out and hit the gym, Swift was less convinced by Jason's proposal.

"I'm walking out of the room, and Taylor's like, 'This is f---ed up.' And I'm just like, 'Nah, it'll be good. It'll be good!' " Travis added as he and Jason cracked up.

Though they weren't pictured together, Jason shared that he and Swift were both at Arrowhead Stadium to cheer on Travis and the Chiefs as they defeated the Los Angeles Chargers.

Sharing that he attended a New Heights tailgate ahead of the game, Jason added, "We were all there in Arrowhead this weekend. It was a blast."

articles.title: Prince Harry Expresses Regret for Final Phone Call With Princess Diana
articles.summary: Nearly 30 years after Princess Diana’s tragic death, Prince Harry admitted that rushing to get off the phone during his and Prince William’s final phone call...
articles.body:
Prince Harry can't let go of his final phone call with Princess Diana .

Nearly 30 years after his mom and her boyfriend Dodi Fayed were killed in a car collision in August 1997, the Duke of Sussex emphasized that he still regrets not giving her more time on his final phone call with her.

"I have spoken very openly about one of my biggest regrets is that last phone call I had with her," Harry told GQ in an interview published Oct. 20 . "If I'd known it was the last call with her, how different that conversation would've been. And I'm the one that has to live with that."

Indeed, as Harry—dad to Archie , 7, and Lilibet , 3, with wife Meghan Markle —recalled of the quick phone call he and brother Prince William had with Diana before the fatal crash in Paris, "All I wanted to do was go off and run and play with my cousins."

The 42-year-old is not the only one who has expressed regret for their final moments with Diana. Similarly, William has previously noted it was just as devastating for him.

"Harry and I were in a desperate rush to say goodbye, you know 'see you later'... If I'd known now obviously what was going to happen I wouldn't have been so blase about it and everything else," the Prince of Wales, who was 15 when Diana died while Harry was 12, shared in the 2017 documentary Diana, Our Mother: Her Life and Legacy. "That phone call sticks in my mind quite heavily."

In the same documentary, Harry emphasized how heavily the loss of their mother at such a young age weighs on both he and his brother.

There's not a day that William and I don't wish that she was still around," he said, "and we wonder what kind of a mother she would be now, and what kind of a public role she would have, and what a difference she would be making."

Meanwhile, Diana's other loved ones have also reflected on how trivial their final moments with her seemed. In his new memoir, Swan Song: Diana, My Sister , Charles Spencer admitted that his final memory with the late Princess of Wales was on her 36th birthday, when they happened to be dining at the same restaurant weeks before her death.

"Neither of us had any idea that the other was going to be at the evening," he wrote. "We had only that brief chat, never to see each other again."

While her time with her loved ones was entirely too short, Diana made an extraordinary impact during her life. Keep reading for a look at how she redefined royalty…

New Approach to the Public's Fascination

Family That Tours Together, Stays Together

For the latest breaking news updates, click here to download the E! News App

images.caption: Anwar Hussein/WireImage

Princess Diana went far against the grain when she advocated for causes previously considered taboo amongst royals, including AIDS research, land mine removal and homelessness in the U.K. She was one of the first public figures to be photographed interacting physically with AIDS victims—a decision that helped destigmatize and lessen the public's fear around the condition.

The paparazzi's role in Princess Diana's tragic passing actually brought the royal family and the press closer than ever before. After her death, the palace made agreements with the British media to ensure photographers wouldn't overstep boundaries in an attempt to satiate public interest. As a result, we see more palace-organized photo calls and greater cooperation on both sides when it comes to balancing privacy and public figuredom.

Perhaps Diana's most extraordinary influence on the royal family was her unprecedented vulnerability in the face of public scrutiny. She openly discussed her struggle with mental health (notably suffering from postpartum depression after giving birth to Prince William), and in her landmark interview with the BBC's Martin Bashir Diana remarked, "Well, maybe I was the first person ever to be in this family who ever had a depression or was ever openly tearful. And obviously that was daunting, because if you've never seen it before how do you support it?" Years later, William and Harry have kept their mother's legacy alive by launching Heads Together , a campaign that works to change the U.K.'s conversation around mental health and wellbeing.

The princess made yet another impact on life behind palace doors by maintaining unusually laid back relationships with the royal staff. Her famously close friendship with butler Paul Burrell captivated headlines, and she reportedly set up play dates for Prince William and Harry with her employees' children. Princess Di also encouraged her sons to participate in the kitchen, which might have inspired Kate Middleton 's decision to often prepare home-cooked meals for her family.

Princess Di flipped the script on traditional royal birthing techniques by welcoming both her children outside Buckingham Palace, where Prince Charles was born decades before. This made Prince William the first future British monarch to be born in a hospital on June 21, 1982. Wills and the Duchess of Cambridge followed suit, welcoming Prince George and Princess Charlotte in the same medical center, St. Mary's in London.

Instead of putting her sons on a pedestal like the entire world had already done, Princess Diana made an effort to create a sense of normalcy for William and Harry. Her youngest explained in an interview, "She made the decision that no matter what, despite all the difficulties of growing up in that lime light and on that stage, she was going to ensure that both of us had as normal life as possible. And if that means taking us for a burger every now and then or sneaking us into the cinema, or driving through the country lanes with the roof down in her old school BMW to listen to Enya ."

When Diana and Prince Charles were to embark on their official tour of Australia and New Zealand in 1983, she insisted that Wills (then only 10-months-old) would join his parents on the road. Royal children never typically traveled on these trips, but Diana's decision to keep her family together explains why Prince George and Princess Charlotte are now always included on overseas ventures .

articles.title: Zélia Duncan oferece 'Pan y leche' em single no rastro do êxito da música de Maurício Pereira no show 'Agudo grave' | G1
articles.body:
Zélia Duncan lança o single 'Pan y leche' amanhã, sexta-feira, 23 de outubro, em gravação produzida e arranjada por Maria Beraldo — Foto: Reprodução /Vídeo

♬ Enquanto ensaiava o show “Agudo grave” sob direção musical de Maria Beraldo, produtora do álbum também intitulado “Agudo grave” (2026) e lançado em maio, Zélia Duncan teve a ideia de gravar “Pan y leche” (1995), canção composta por Maurício Pereira e lançada na voz do autor há 31 anos em gravação feita para o álbum “Na tradição” (1995).

Com letra em português, mas alguns versos em espanhol, a canção “Pan y leche” não faz parte do repertório do álbum “Agudo grave” , mas entrou no roteiro do show por sugestão de Maria Beraldo, feita diante da intenção de Zélia de incluir no espetáculo uma música que dialogasse com o momento social do Brasil.

Cantada já perto do fim do show, a música “Pan y leche” se tornou um dos números mais aplaudidos das apresentações de “Agudo grave” em São Paulo (SP) e no Rio de Janeiro (RJ).

No rastro dessa ótima receptividade da música de Maurício Pereira na releitura da cantora, Zélia Duncan lança amanhã, sexta-feira, 23 de outubro, o single com a gravação de “Pan y leche”, feita em estúdio com produção musical, arranjo e o sopro do clarone de Maria Beraldo.

Além de Beraldo, a cantora dá voz a “Pan y leche” com os toques dos músicos Amanda Camargo (piano e vocais), Biel Basile (bateria), Ciro Belluci (flauta e vocais) e Fábio Sá (baixo e vocais). Tó Brandileone assina a engenharia de som do single mixado por Ricardo Mosca e masterizado por Carlos Freitas.

O single “Pan y leche” chega ao mercado fonográfico digital em edição do selo Duncan Discos. Já o clipe homônimo tem direção de Elisa Mendes e Pedro Colombo.

articles.title: Diretora de presídio é afastada por desvio de alimentos no RJ | G1
articles.standfirst: Graça Maria Silva de Souza foi autuada em flagrante por peculato e exonerada da função.
articles.summary: Graça Maria Silva de Souza foi autuada em flagrante por peculato e exonerada após desvio de alimentos no Instituto Penal Oscar Stevenson, em Benfica.
articles.body:
Graça Maria Silva de Souza , diretora do Instituto Penal Oscar Stevenson, em Benfica, na Zona Norte do Rio de Janeiro , foi afastada por suspeita de desviar alimentos do estabelecimento .

Durante uma abordagem ao veículo da diretora, foram encontrados no porta-malas carne, frango, peixe, linguiça, queijos, frutas, óleo, leite, café e achocolatados .

Segundo a Secretaria Estadual de Polícia Penal (Seppen), ela foi autuada em flagrante por peculato na 21ª DP (Bonsucesso). A servidora também foi exonerada , e um processo administrativo disciplinar foi instaurado.

A TV Globo não conseguiu contato com a defesa de Glória.

Graça Maria Silva de Souza — Foto: Reprodução

A ação ocorreu após uma denúncia sobre irregularidades na destinação de alimentos do presídio. A Subsecretaria de Inteligência do Sistema Penitenciário (Ssispen) e a Corregedoria da Seppen passaram a monitorar o caso.

De acordo com as investigações, uma equipe da Ssispen foi acionada para verificar a presença de um veículo nas proximidades do presídio. Ao abrir o carro, que era de Glória, encontraram os alimentos. A revista foi feita na presença da servidora .

Ainda segundo as investigações, ao ser questionada sobre a origem dos produtos e a documentação, Graça afirmou que não tinha nota fiscal nem outro comprovante . Ela declarou que os alimentos haviam sido arrecadados no presídio porque não seriam mais consumidos e que seriam destinados a um centro espírita .

A servidora, o veículo e os alimentos foram encaminhados à 21ª DP.

Em nota, a Seppen afirmou que “não compactua com quaisquer desvios de conduta e cometimento de crimes praticados por seus servidores” e que mantém atuação no combate a essas práticas por meio da Corregedoria e da Ssispen.

Instituto Penal Oscar Stevenson, em Benfica — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

articles.title: 'Jailer 2' box office collection day 7: Rajinikanth, Mohanlal and Nelson Dilipkumar film earns Rs 582.45 cr worldwide; India Net collection crosses Rs 300 cr
articles.summary: 'Jailer 2', starring Rajinikanth and Mohanlal, witnessed a decline in box office collections on its seventh day in theaters.
articles.body: 'Jailer 2', starring Rajinikanth and Mohanlal, witnessed a decline in box office collections on its seventh day in theaters. The action drama earned Rs 28.15 cr in India net collections on Wednesday, October 21. This represented a 39.9% drop from the previous day's Rs 46.80 cr. According to Sacnilk, the film has crossed the Rs 300 cr milestone in domestic net earnings, while its worldwide gross collection has reached Rs 582.45 cr.Jailer 2 Movie ReviewThe film's India gross collection stands at Rs 371.45 cr, with domestic net earnings totaling Rs 317.20 cr. Overseas markets contributed Rs 7 cr on Wednesday, taking the cumulative overseas gross to Rs 211 cr. The film's seventh-day performance came after several days of substantial theatrical earnings across multiple language versions.'Jailer 2' day 7 language-wise collectionThe Tamil version led the domestic box office on Wednesday, earning Rs 18.50 cr from 6,914 shows. The Telugu version collected Rs 6 cr across 2,187 screenings. articles.title: ‘Clayface’ Twitter Reviews: Tom Rhys Harries’ body horror hailed as best villain origin story since ‘The Joker’
articles.summary: DC Studios’ first-ever horror film, ‘Clayface’, is all set to usher in spooky season as it debuts in theatres on Friday, October 23.
articles.body: DC Studios’ first-ever horror film, ‘Clayface’, is all set to usher in spooky season as it debuts in theatres on Friday, October 23. Ahead of the highly anticipated release, the film has received a largely positive response from early viewers, with social media reactions praising Tom Rhys Harries’ performance, the film's disturbing body-horror sequences and its tragic take on one of Batman’s most recognisable villains. While some viewers have called it the 'best DC film since The Joker’, others have pointed to issues with its third act and tonal inconsistencies.'Clayface' debuts with 77% ratingThe film’s Rotten Tomatoes score has reportedly debuted at 77%, placing it behind ‘Superman’, which stands at 83%, and ahead of ‘Supergirl’ at 52%. The early reactions suggest that director James Watkins’ take on the character leans heavily into grotesque imagery and psychological horror rather than the conventional superhero formula.'Clayface' early Twitter reviewsOne viewer praised the film saying, "Clayface is, without a doubt, a BODY HORROR, and a damn good one! A macabre, visceral, and very well-constructed movie. Tom Rhys is SENSATIONAL as Matt Hagen, just like Naomi Ackie, who delivers an excellent performance as Dr. Caitlin Bates."Another viewer wrote "I really dug this! The film is so well paced & immediately hooks you into Matt Hagen’s tragic story. DCU’s Gotham feels as grimy & alive as I could hope. The body horror is GNARLY. Coming from someone who HATES the solo villain movie trend I was pretty happy with this!"Another reaction celebrated the film for embracing tragic villains rather than turning them into conventional antiheroes, writing that ‘Clayface’ “reminds you why Batman villains are different”.The film’s body horror has emerged as one of its biggest talking points. One viewer wrote "Clayface is a bold villain origin story. It's shockingly dark , brutal and twisted but also best DC movie since The Joker. Some scenes are hard to watch for me but even I closed my eyes, I can hear the shocking reaction from the audiences. OMG throughout the whole movie :) The reactions from the crowds are awesome. It did remind me of The Substance, but much more. Would definitely be interested in seeing this character in more DC movies. It's really kind of sad to see Tom Rhys Harries' pretty face got destroyed every few mins. He embraced this role quite well."Another wrote, "Clayface is everything you want from a villain led movie. No more anti hero Bs, DC understands that tragic Villains can exist. I was harsh with Lanterns and Supergirl so I went into this movie excited, but nervous. This movie reminds you why Batman villains are different."Still another said, "They actually made a comic book movie that feels dangerous, awkward and whatnot. The body horror is genuinely disturbing, with some insanely creative sequences, but beneath all the gore lies a tragic story with a gothic soul. Tom Rhys Harries really sells Matt Hagen’s slow descent, making you feel for a guy who’s becoming something truly monstrous. Overall, it is Messy, disturbing and unimaginably tragic."What is ‘Clayface’ about?However, the response has not been entirely unanimous. One viewer called ‘Clayface’ an “entertaining but frustrating tragedy”. The tweet read "Clayface is an entertaining but frustrating tragedy that left me craving SO MUCH MORE! A brutal blend of grotesque body horror and a heartbreaking character study, with BRILLIANT performances from Tom Rhys Harries and Naomi Ackie.Unfortunately, the third act lost me with cheesy dialogue, questionable choices, and some jarring tonal shifts. Don’t even get me started on those mobsters LOL. The film comes SO CLOSE to balancing tragedy, brutality, and campiness."Another wrote, "Clayface was pretty gnarly in places with a great score. My main issue is it never fully settles in if it wants to be a body horror or a cartoon. The gore effects are pretty well done and one sequence had me hiding behind my hands."Directed by James Watkins, ‘Clayface’ features a screenplay by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini, from a story by Flanagan, based on characters from DC.The film follows Matt Hagen, whose rise from a street kid in Gotham to a Hollywood leading man is cut short when the actions of a local crime boss leave him horribly disfigured. Abandoned by his team, Hagen turns to an experimental treatment that miraculously restores his appearance but brings troubling physical and psychological side effects. As his condition deteriorates, he embarks on a destructive path driven by revenge.Alongside Harries and Ackie, the cast includes David Dencik, Max Minghella, Eddie Marsan, Nancy Carroll and Joshua James.‘Clayface’ is scheduled to release in cinemas across India on October 23, 2026, in English and Hindi.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Could Reds poach Guardians coach? "(Francona) would be the reason" why
articles.summary: Former Cincinnati Reds pitcher Carl Willis spent six seasons as Terry Francona's pitching coach in Cleveland and values "how much better he made me."
articles.body:
Can the Cincinnati Reds steal some secrets from the small-market trio that made up the last three teams standing in the playoff field this month?

Or maybe just steal one of their pitching coaches?

Cleveland Guardians pitching coach Carl Willis said he's not sure what kind of fit he might be with the Reds at this point in his career.

But his track record and relationship with Reds manager Terry Francona make him perhaps the most obvious outside candidate to consider for a team with a lot of ground to make up and a short window with its talented core and high-profile manager.

"Cleveland means a lot to me. This organization has been so good to me," said Willis, who has spent 16 seasons — including the past nine consecutively – guiding the Cleveland's top-flight pitching staff at the big-league level.

"But I'll also tell you that Tito has been very, very good to me as well," Willis added. "I tell him all the time how much better he made me, just the experience I had with him, the trust he put in me."

Francona and Willis spent six seasons together in Cleveland, winning three AL Central titles.

As the Reds continue the process of replacing former pitching coach Derek Johnson , Willis became available for interviews this week after the Guardians were eliminated in the American League Championship Series by the Rays.

Willis, 65, has worked in recent years on a year-to-year agreement with the Guardians, reserving the freedom to decide at the end of each season what he might want to do next.

"I've kind of told the organization the last couple of years that I need to get to the end of the year and think about it," said Willis, who pitched in the majors for nine years, including 40 relief appearances for the Reds over the 1985 and '86 seasons. "But I don't know the best thing for me or another organization, if they were interested in pursuing that – going somewhere new knowing that you're feeling like you're kind of year-to-year, I don't know if that's fair to anybody.

"If that were to happen, and then all of a sudden they're back to a new potential philosophy or whatever … I'm pretty happy with where I'm at, and we'll see what happens."

The other side of the career-timing issue Willis raised is that he and Francona are roughly the same age, have the longstanding relationship that should mean a seamless transition, and it might be reasonable to expect Willis to stick around as long as Francona does.

Francona has one more guaranteed year left on his contract, plus an club option for 2028.

The Guardians have finished among the top five in American League team ERA seven of the past nine seasons with Willis as the pitching coach and has been part of helping set an MLB standard for developing big-league pitchers, including working with CC Sabathia, Cliff Lee, Corey Kluber and Shane Bieber along the way.

The Reds have interviewed in-house candidates Matt Tracy and Oscar Marin for the pitching coach job and this week were still considering potential outside candidates.

That process might accelerate with only the Brewers and Rays still playing.

Willis didn't know how he might fit into that process or even whether a change to the other team in Ohio would work for him. But Francona admittedly is the wild card for his part in it.

"I can truthfully tell you: I'm not saying I would even consider it, but if I were to, he would be the reason," Willis said.

articles.summary: Former Cincinnati Reds pitcher Carl Willis spent six seasons as Terry Francona's pitching coach in Cleveland and values "how much better he made me."
articles.body:
Can the Cincinnati Reds steal some secrets from the small-market trio that made up the last three teams standing in the playoff field this month?

Or maybe just steal one of their pitching coaches?

Cleveland Guardians pitching coach Carl Willis said he's not sure what kind of fit he might be with the Reds at this point in his career.

But his track record and relationship with Reds manager Terry Francona make him perhaps the most obvious outside candidate to consider for a team with a lot of ground to make up and a short window with its talented core and high-profile manager.

"Cleveland means a lot to me. This organization has been so good to me," said Willis, who has spent 16 seasons — including the past nine consecutively – guiding the Cleveland's top-flight pitching staff at the big-league level.

"But I'll also tell you that Tito has been very, very good to me as well," Willis added. "I tell him all the time how much better he made me, just the experience I had with him, the trust he put in me."

Francona and Willis spent six seasons together in Cleveland, winning three AL Central titles.

As the Reds continue the process of replacing former pitching coach Derek Johnson , Willis became available for interviews this week after the Guardians were eliminated in the American League Championship Series by the Rays.

Willis, 65, has worked in recent years on a year-to-year agreement with the Guardians, reserving the freedom to decide at the end of each season what he might want to do next.

"I've kind of told the organization the last couple of years that I need to get to the end of the year and think about it," said Willis, who pitched in the majors for nine years, including 40 relief appearances for the Reds over the 1985 and '86 seasons. "But I don't know the best thing for me or another organization, if they were interested in pursuing that – going somewhere new knowing that you're feeling like you're kind of year-to-year, I don't know if that's fair to anybody.

"If that were to happen, and then all of a sudden they're back to a new potential philosophy or whatever … I'm pretty happy with where I'm at, and we'll see what happens."

The other side of the career-timing issue Willis raised is that he and Francona are roughly the same age, have the longstanding relationship that should mean a seamless transition, and it might be reasonable to expect Willis to stick around as long as Francona does.

Francona has one more guaranteed year left on his contract, plus an club option for 2028.

The Guardians have finished among the top five in American League team ERA seven of the past nine seasons with Willis as the pitching coach and has been part of helping set an MLB standard for developing big-league pitchers, including working with CC Sabathia, Cliff Lee, Corey Kluber and Shane Bieber along the way.

The Reds have interviewed in-house candidates Matt Tracy and Oscar Marin for the pitching coach job and this week were still considering potential outside candidates.

That process might accelerate with only the Brewers and Rays still playing.

Willis didn't know how he might fit into that process or even whether a change to the other team in Ohio would work for him. But Francona admittedly is the wild card for his part in it.

"I can truthfully tell you: I'm not saying I would even consider it, but if I were to, he would be the reason," Willis said.

articles.title: Derry International Choir Festival: Singers from across the world at event
articles.summary: The festival brings together hundreds of local singers and community groups alongside international choirs.
articles.body:
More than 100 choirs from around the world are arriving in Londonderry for one of the UK's largest choral festivals.

Choristers from Sweden, Estonia, France, Germany, the UK and Ireland will rub shoulders with local singers of all ages for the four-day City of Derry International Choir Festival.

Now in its 14th year, a record number of choirs are taking part with a variety of performances and competitions.

It opens on Thursday with a gala concert at the Millennium Forum, featuring the Ulster Orchestra and Festival Chorus under the direction of newly-appointed chief conductor Anna Handler.

Entitled Beethoven – Triumph & Transcendence, the concert will also feature soloists Gemma Summerfield, Ryan Vaughan Davies and Alex Birkus.

Handler told BBC New NI the Derry festival's growth is testament to the power of live choral music to bring people together.

"People come because they want to hear real performance. They want to see human engagement but also human trial," she said.

"When you see people doing something that they love, when you see their passion and when you see their engagement…. You can not get that through listening on headphones or through streaming music," Handler, who is making her festival debut, added.

Opening night, she said, will see "three amazing soloists, soprano, tenor and bass, a great chorus and very agile and vital orchestra" grace the Millennium Forum stage.

The audience can expect "energy as well as reflection and introspection", the German-Colombian conductor said, adding she knows a Derry audience will be as "warm and welcoming" as they have been when she has conducted previously in the city.

"It is very exciting to be back, much of the opening night programme is now not often performed," she said.

On Friday, Grammy-nominated vocal ensemble Tenebrae will perform at the Guildhall, followed by a late-night concert at the historic St Columb's Cathedral featuring The Apex Singers and their distinctive eight-part a cappella folk arrangements.

The Oak Tree of Derry International Competition will take place at the Guildhall on Saturday, bringing some of the festival's leading visiting choirs together to compete.

The event will conclude on Sunday with a closing gala and awards ceremony at the Millennium Forum.

Speaking to BBC Radio Foyle's North West Today programme , festival director Dónal Doherty said the key to its success was community involvement.

"There's over 100 choirs in the festival altogether and 60 of those will be performing as part of the community programme.

"It's incredible and that's going to happen throughout Derry, Limavady, Strabane, Donegal with a choral trail and concerts in Letterkenny as well, this year developing on last year's choral trail.

"There will be pop-up performances throughout the city as well as concerts in community centres and in care homes and it's just incredible."

The event was born out of Derry's year as City of Culture in 2013 and Doherty said was now reaching a global audience while becoming increasingly embedded in the community each year.

"The international choirs that we have performing, their conductors, their members, the international panel of adjudicators, we work very hard to make sure that they become advocates of the festival, wherever they go back to throughout the world and promote the festival and that's what we're beginning to see," he said.

"We're beginning to see choirs now putting 'Derry October' into their calendar and for international choirs, in fact for any choirs to travel to Derry, it must be planned not a year in advance," he said, explaining many choirs are showing interest two or three years ahead of the event.

That indicates a "maturing" of the festival, he said.

"It's evidence also of genuinely the word going out that this is a quality festival and it's a beautiful place to come to - whatever the weather - and in terms of the welcome that they're guaranteed, which has been a consistent message from 2013 in our first festival, the warmth of the welcome is special."

Choir's 25 years a testament to 'talent and commitment'

Choir festival 'the biggest yet', say organisers

Choirs descend on Derry for international festival

images.caption: Dónal Doherty says the annual event has gone from strength-to-strength since it first started back in 2013

articles.title: Sale a subasta este 'Coche Fantástico' personal de David Hasselhoff que nunca apareció en la serie
articles.standfirst: El coche es un ejemplar de KITT que el actor guardó durante años y que en 1999 fue robado en Italia. Este 7 de noviembre será subastado y se prevé un precio de venta superior al medio millón de euros
articles.summary: El coche es un ejemplar de KITT que el actor guardó durante años y que en 1999 fue robado en Italia. Este 7 de noviembre será subastado y se prevé un precio de venta superior al medio millón de euros
articles.body: Una luz roja recorriendo el morro, un salpicadero repleto de pantallas y botones luminosos y una voz que respondía al conductor. Para millones de chavales de los años ochenta, KITT era mucho más que un coche: era una máquina con la que todos habríamos deseado salir a perseguir a los malos. El coche fantástico se estrenó en España el 1 de agosto de 1985, en la sobremesa de TVE. En ella, David Hasselhoff interpretaba a Michael Knight, un hombre dado por muerto que recibía una nueva identidad y se convertía en una especie de justiciero. A su lado tenía al auténtico protagonista de la serie, a KITT (su auténtico nombre era Knight Industries 2.000), un coche capaz de hablar, de tomar decisiones y de conducir por su cuenta cuando nadie había oído hablar ni de la conducción autónoma ni de la inteligencia artificial. La fórmula impresionó a una generación de jovencitos en todo el mundo. En una época en la que los ordenadores de casa eran los Spectrum, Amstrad o Commodore, aquel Pontiac negro parecía anticipar un futuro que todavía quedaba muy lejos. Hoy, cuatro décadas después, el coche sigue siendo un mito para los cuarentones y cincuentones que crecieron pegados al televisor. Y los ejemplares que se conservan, tanto los empleados en el rodaje como los preparados para promocionar la serie, son piezas codiciadas por coleccionistas y aficionados. No es extraño que algunas unidades de estos coches hayan alcanzado cifras bastante altas en las subastas. En 2020, un KITT utilizado en giras promocionales de la serie y en el Night Rocker Tour de Hasselhoff en Austria se vendió por 169.000 euros. En enero de 2021, otra unidad, en este caso propiedad de Hasselhoff, alcanzó los 285.000 euros pese a que tampoco había participado nunca en el rodaje. Y este último caso es muy parecido al del modelo que acaba de salir a la luz, porque también fue propiedad personal del actor y lo acompañó por una gira promocional por Europa, aunque nunca apareciera en la serie. La base elegida para crear el coche fantástico fue un Pontiac Firebird Trans Am de 1982, uno de esos deportivos estadounidenses de motor enorme que se bebían el depósito a ritmo vertiginoso. Durante las cuatro temporadas de la serie se emplearon alrededor de 17 coches, todos adaptados para desempeñar distintas funciones durante la producción (los había para saltos y derrapes, para primeros planos...) El motor era un V8 de 5,0 litros con inyección Cross-Fire que desarrollaba 165 CV y permitía al coche alcanzar 195 km/h, cifra respetable para un deportivo americano de principios de los ochenta (pero mucho más terrenal que las prestaciones que se atribuían a KITT en la ficción). En Estados Unidos, el Trans Am partía de 9.658 dólares de la época, equivalentes a unos 8.600 euros al cambio. Pero el coche que los niños de los años 80 veíamos en la tele tenía cambios respecto al modelo de concesionario. El diseñador Michael Scheffe dio forma a su característica carrocería negra, con una inolvidable luz oscilante de color rojo que parecía escanear la carretera. También se modificaron los faldones, el alerón y los pilotos traseros, oscurecidos para reforzar su aspecto futurista. Pero el verdadero espectáculo estaba dentro: un volante de dos brazos similar al de un avión, una consola central llena de botones, pantallas de las de tubo de imagen, indicadores luminosos y sistemas de control que convertían el habitáculo en una nave espacial de bolsillo. Además, su carrocería estaba protegida por un blindaje molecular casi indestructible, capaz de resistir disparos y explosiones sin siquiera sufrir un arañazo. Por supuesto, esas capacidades pertenecían a la ficción, aunque ayudaron a convertir el coche en un icono tecnológico cuya voz original puso el actor William Daniels. El Coche Fantástico que ahora sale a subasta en Zúrich es un Trans Am de 1982 transformado por Thomas J. Oberhaus, de Hollywood Productions, siguiendo los planos originales de Universal Pictures. La documentación lo identifica como uno de los coches utilizados para acompañar a Hasselhoff en apariciones televisivas, conciertos, exposiciones y actos promocionales por Europa. No se trata, por tanto, de uno de los vehículos que aparecieron en los episodios, pero tampoco de una de tantas réplicas más o menos fieles al original. De hecho, un certificado de autenticidad expedido por AMELI CAR AG el 29 de diciembre de 1989 recoge su transformación y su vinculación con el actor. También consta su aparición en la televisión suiza el 26 de noviembre de 1990, cuando el presentador Beni Thurnherr condujo el coche hasta el estudio. Su historial incluye hasta un episodio real digno de la propia serie, ya que durante la década de los noventa, cuando pertenecía a la discográfica suiza Exclusa AG, el coche fue robado en Italia. Por suerte, la Interpol pudo recuperarlo, aunque los ladrones se llevaron parte de la electrónica original del salpicadero. El coche mantiene la estructura original del salpicadero de su conversión, el volante característico, los mandos, la consola y el conjunto central con la botonera. Los componentes electrónicos que faltaban fueron sustituidos por otros de estilo similar al de las primeras temporadas, con módulo de voz y dos pantallas LOTI. Y en el exterior conserva la luz roja del frontal, de accionamiento remoto, y los pilotos oscurecidos con cubiertas de plexiglás. La unidad se encuentra en estado funcional, aunque sus modificaciones impiden utilizarla legalmente en vías públicas. Se entregará con el certificado de AMELI CAR AG, documentación aduanera de época, la factura de compraventa de 1999 (cuando lo compró su actual propietario), fotografías históricas junto a Hasselhoff, carteles dedicados de El coche fantástico, modelos a escala en sus cajas y retratos en blanco y negro del actor. La subasta será el próximo sábado 7 de noviembre y la organiza Broad Arrow Auctions en Suiza. La estimación habla de que alguien pagará entre 270.000 y 539.000 euros. Y podemos estar seguros de que el máximo pujador será uno de aquellos chiquillos que se quedaba pegado al televisor viendo la serie.

images.caption: El salpicadero del coche era un derroche de electrónica. Instagram/ @knigh_rider_official_

articles.title: Carlos Boyero, crítico de cine, sobre Pedro Almodóvar y el éxito de 'La bola negra': "Cuando los egos andan disparados..."
articles.standfirst: Carlos Boyero celebra el éxito nacional e internacional de 'La bola negra' y de Los Javis
articles.summary: Carlos Boyero celebra el éxito nacional e internacional de 'La bola negra' y de Los Javis
articles.body: Carlos Boyero ha vuelto a protagonizar un intercambio cargado de ironía en 'La ventana del cine', el programa de la Cadena SER presentado por Carles Francino. El crítico cinematográfico ha celebrado el éxito nacional e internacional de 'La bola negra', la película de Javier Calvo y Javier Ambrossi, conocidos como Los Javis, antes de deslizar que hay alguien que podría no estar llevando demasiado bien el triunfo de los cineastas. Francino no ha tardado en plantearle un nombre: Pedro Almodóvar. "Y me alegro mucho del triunfo nacional e internacional de los Javis. Y sé de alguien, pero eso son cosas mías, que se puede estar muriéndose de envidia, así, con el éxito de estos chicos", ha afirmado Boyero durante su intervención en el espacio radiofónico. La frase ha provocado la reacción inmediata del presentador, que le ha preguntado si realmente cree que alguien puede sentir envidia por el momento profesional que atraviesan los dos directores. Boyero ha mantenido su insinuación y ha continuado con una reflexión sobre los egos en la industria audiovisual. "Cuando los egos andan disparados y además te los están masajeando todo el rato y estás convencido de que eres el único genial y grandioso y que te mereces todo, pues igual no te sienta bien", ha comentado el crítico. Aunque Boyero no ha pronunciado ningún nombre, Francino ha querido ir un paso más allá y le ha preguntado directamente si se refería a Pedro Almodóvar. "¿Pero tú crees que Almodóvar, que está aquí?", ha planteado el presentador, que después ha recordado que el cineasta manchego está implicado en la producción de 'La bola negra'. "Sí, es productor", ha señalado Francino. Boyero, por su parte, ha respondido con una frase que mantiene el tono irónico de la conversación: "Tiene un corazón de oro y una generosidad infinita". El crítico ha añadido que Almodóvar y Los Javis mantienen una relación de admiración mutua. Para justificarlo, ha recordado la admiración que los dos directores han expresado hacia el cineasta manchego a lo largo de su trayectoria. "Le dedicaron una serie infame ahí en Movistar de no sé cuántos capítulos, exaltando su personalidad y su mundo como si no existiera otro en esta tierra", ha comentado Boyero, en una intervención marcada por su habitual tono mordaz. Francino ha insistido en que la referencia había quedado clara para los oyentes: "Bueno, pero todo el mundo lo ha entendido", ha replicado cuando Boyero recalcó que él no había mencionado a Almodóvar. Este, sin embargo, ha mantenido la ambigüedad y ha cerrado el intercambio con otra frase irónica: "Pero yo es que tengo mucha imaginación cuando quiero, Carlos". "Viva la ironía", ha respondido Francino.

articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh denied permission by Delhi Police for his concert on October 30 at Jawaharlal Nehru stadium over security concerns
articles.summary: Delhi Police have denied permission for Diljit Dosanjh’s scheduled concert at Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) Stadium in New Delhi on October 30, citing security
articles.body: Delhi Police have denied permission for Diljit Dosanjh’s scheduled concert at Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) Stadium in New Delhi on October 30, citing security concerns, according to ANI. The decision has cast uncertainty over the Delhi leg of the singer’s Aura India Tour, with the police reportedly withholding clearance following a review of the organisers’ request.According to ANI, a letter reportedly issued by the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), South Delhi, and addressed to a ticketing platform cited threat-related inputs, security requirements during the festive season and other law and order concerns as reasons for rejecting the request.The police have not publicly provided further details about the specific security inputs that led to the decision. It is also unclear whether the organisers will seek fresh permission or explore the possibility of rescheduling the concert or shifting it to another venue.The development comes as fans await Dosanjh’s performance in the national capital. The singer, who has established a strong following in India and overseas, is known for his energetic live shows and performances at major international venues.Dosanjh has performed at renowned venues, including Madison Square Garden in New York and Wembley Stadium in London. He also became the first Punjabi artiste to headline and sell out Wembley Stadium, marking a significant milestone for Punjabi music on the international stage.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 sees surge in home upgrades, demand grows beyond metros
articles.summary: Home upgrades have emerged as one of the biggest shopping trends during the ongoing Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026, with shopping volumes growing more
articles.body: Home upgrades have emerged as one of the biggest shopping trends during the ongoing Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026, with shopping volumes growing more than threefold as consumers invest in kitchen appliances, smart home products, entertainment devices and large household appliances ahead of Diwali.According to Amazon India, growth is increasingly being driven by smaller cities, with non-metro markets accounting for more than 60% of shopping volumes and expanding at twice the rate of metro cities. Cities such as Lucknow, Jaipur, Patna, Guwahati, Coimbatore, Nagpur, Indore and Kochi are leading demand, as customers increasingly explore new product categories and upgrade to premium appliances.Commenting on the trend, Aman Deep Lohan, Director, Home, Kitchen and Outdoors at Amazon India, said consumers are showing growing confidence in upgrading their homes with technology-focused products, while affordability options such as no-cost EMI, exchange offers and instant bank discounts are helping shoppers make larger purchases.According to the company, AI-powered cooking appliances, robotic vacuum cleaners, air purifiers and connected lighting products are among the key categories witnessing increased demand during the festive sale.Amazon also highlighted the role of its AI shopping assistant Rufus, which allows customers to search for products using natural language queries in multiple Indian languages, including Hinglish.Air fryers, refrigerators and dishwashers see strong growthThe company said the kitchen appliances category is currently growing at 3.4 times its average daily pace, with smart and small appliances recording growth of 4.5 times. Air fryers have emerged among the fastest-growing products, operating at 7.5 times their average-day sales pace, while ovens are growing at 5.2 times. Brands such as Philips and SharkNinja have reported growth of more than seven times compared with regular sales periods. Premium refrigerators are also witnessing strong traction. Refrigerators with capacities above 300 litres are selling at 34 times their average-day pace, led by frost-free and side-by-side models from Samsung, LG, Haier and Bosch. Amazon said the Samsung 653-litre AI-enabled side-by-side refrigerator is operating at 33 times its average-day pace.Other lifestyle-oriented kitchen categories are gaining momentum as well, with dishwashers growing sevenfold and chimneys sixfold compared with normal sales levels.Smart TVs, robotic cleaners and connected lighting gain popularityThe living room category is also seeing significant upgrades as consumers opt for larger screens and connected devices. According to Amazon, home entertainment products, including smart TVs and speakers, are running at 37 times their average-day sales pace, with smart TVs accounting for nearly 65% of the category's growth.Brands including Samsung, Xiaomi and TCL have collectively grown 56 times compared with average sales levels, while Indian brand Lumio recorded a 42-fold increase. Robotic vacuum cleaners are another fast-growing category, with sales running at 9.2 times normal levels. Brands such as Ecovacs and Dreame are among the key beneficiaries of this trend. Demand for air purifiers has increased 5.2 times, while smart fans have grown fourfold. Indian smart fan maker Atomberg has reported a fivefold increase in sales during the festive period. Connected lighting products from brands including Philips and Wipro are also seeing strong demand as consumers prepare their homes for Diwali celebrations.Premium appliances and financing options fuel upgradesAmazon said customers are increasingly upgrading to premium and energy-efficient appliances rather than simply replacing existing products. Home appliance sales have grown 25 times during the early stages of the festival sale. Washer-dryers are growing at 18 times their average pace, while premium front-load washing machines continue to gain popularity. LG emerged as the best-selling washing machine brand, recording 17 times its regular-day sales.Air conditioners with four-star and five-star energy ratings are also witnessing strong adoption, growing 15 times faster than normal sales levels. Brands such as Panasonic, Hitachi and Daikin are among the leading sellers in the category. The company said financing options, including exchange discounts, instant bank offers and no-cost EMI plans starting at ₹99 per day, are helping drive the premiumisation trend.AI tools helping customers discover productsAmazon said more than six million customers have used its Deal Alerts feature, which allows shoppers to track prices and receive notifications when products reach preferred price points. The company has also expanded AI-powered shopping tools, including Rufus, Lens AI, AI Review Highlights, Quick View, Buying Guides and personalised product recommendations, to simplify product discovery and comparison.Festival offers continue through DiwaliThe Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 sale will continue throughout the festive season, with the company offering discounts of up to 50% on more than one lakh products and its lowest prices of the year on over two lakh products across categories including Home, Kitchen, Toys and Outdoors. Customers can also avail a 10% instant discount on purchases made using Axis Bank and ICICI Bank credit cards and EMI transactions, along with additional benefits for Prime members and Amazon Pay users.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Vijay was very emotional and spoke to our family’: Srikanth Deva thanks Tamil Nadu CM for state honours to late father Deva, recalls emotional condolence visit
articles.summary: Music composer Srikanth Deva has expressed gratitude to Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and the state government for according state honours to
articles.body: Music composer Srikanth Deva has expressed gratitude to Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and the state government for according state honours to his late father, veteran music composer Deva. In an emotional video message, Srikanth spoke about the family’s grief and recalled Vijay’s personal visit to their home to offer condolences. Deva, popularly known as ‘Thenisai Thendral’, died following a heart attack on October 17 and was laid to rest with state honours at his native village in Ranipet district.‘State honours are not an ordinary thing,’ says Srikanth DevaThanking the Chief Minister and the Tamil Nadu government for the recognition, Srikanth said his father’s death had come as a tremendous shock to the family. He also highlighted the significance of the honour, given Deva’s contribution to the music industry over four decades.“My father’s death has come as a huge shock to us. Even now, we are unable to believe whether it is really true or not. We are going through a lot of pain. At this time, I would like to thank Chief Minister Joseph Vijay and the Tamil Nadu government for giving my father state honours. It is a great recognition for the 40 years he spent in the music industry. State honours are not an ordinary thing,” Srikanth said.His words reflected the family’s gratitude for the government’s gesture and the recognition of Deva’s contribution to Tamil cinema. The state honours were announced in acknowledgement of the veteran composer’s service to music.Srikanth Deva recalls CM Vijay’s emotional visit to their homeSrikanth also thanked ministers, political leaders, members of the film industry and the public for supporting the family during its period of mourning. Recalling Vijay’s visit to their residence, the composer said the Chief Minister personally paid his respects and spoke to the family with concern.“Vijay sir came directly to our house to see my father. He was very emotional and spoke to our family with great concern,” Srikanth recalled.He also shared the words Vijay offered him during the visit.“He told me, ‘Even I am unable to bear this, Srikanth. How are you going to bear it?’ When he was getting into his car, he told me, ‘Ask me if you need anything, Sri,’” he said.Srikanth’s account offered a glimpse into the personal support the family received from the Chief Minister as they coped with the loss of the veteran composer.Deva laid to rest with state honours in his native villageDeva’s death on October 17 prompted an outpouring of tributes from political leaders, actors, musicians and fans. Rajinikanth and Kamal Haasan were among the film personalities who paid their last respects to the composer at his Chennai residence. Several political leaders also mourned his demise. Following the tributes in Chennai, Deva’s mortal remains were taken to his native village in Ranipet district for the final rites. He was laid to rest with state honours at his family’s farmland in Sakkaramallur, near Arcot. The ceremony included a 72-gun salute as a mark of respect for his contribution to the music industry.Known popularly as ‘Thenisai Thendral’, Deva built a career spanning several decades and composed music for hundreds of films across South Indian languages. His work, including memorable compositions for Tamil cinema, earned him a lasting place in the industry.Concluding his emotional message, Srikanth thanked everyone who stood by the family during the difficult period.“On behalf of my father and our entire family, I extend my heartfelt thanks to all the kind-hearted people who stood by us during this painful time,” he said.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Ramayana’ advance booking: Ranbir Kapoor starrer earns Rs 7.41 crore gross, sells 1.3 lakh tickets, prices go up to Rs 3,000
articles.summary: Advance bookings for Ranbir Kapoor's upcoming epic ‘Ramayana: The Rise of a Legend’ directed by Nitesh Tiwari has opened on October 20, coinciding with
articles.body: Advance bookings for Ranbir Kapoor's upcoming epic ‘Ramayana: The Rise of a Legend’ directed by Nitesh Tiwari has opened on October 20, coinciding with Dussehra. The ticket prices are ranging from Rs 200 to over Rs 3,000 across select theatres. While the most affordable tickets are available for the Kannada version in Bengaluru, premium recliner seats for IMAX screenings in Mumbai have been listed at Rs 3,170, making the film’s ticket pricing a talking point ahead of its theatrical release.According to Variety India, the lowest-priced ticket was listed at Rs 200 at KRG Soundarya Mahal in Doddaballapura, Bengaluru, for the Kannada version. At the higher end, a premium recliner seat for an IMAX screening at PVR ICON, Phoenix Palladium, in Mumbai’s Lower Parel was priced at Rs 3,170.Ticket rates differ depending on the city, cinema, language, seat category and screening format. In Bengaluru, tickets for select 2D and 3D shows were reportedly priced between Rs 450 and Rs 950. In Delhi, a 9 am 3D screening at PVR ECX Chanakya Puri was listed at approximately Rs 339 to Rs 407, excluding GST.In Mumbai, tickets for a 7:30 am IMAX 3D show at EROS INOX IMAX Cinema in Churchgate were priced between Rs 530 and Rs 680. Meanwhile, those looking to watch the film from premium recliner seats at PVR ICON, Phoenix Palladium, would have to pay Rs 3,170 for an IMAX screening.These figures are based on reported ticket listings and may vary with showtimes, seat availability, taxes and booking-platform charges. Advance bookings may also open at different times across theatres and language versions.Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, ‘Ramayana: The Rise of a Legend’ is scheduled to arrive in theatres worldwide on November 5, 2026, during the Diwali period. Planned as the first instalment of a two-part cinematic saga inspired by the Hindu epic, the film features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman.The ensemble cast also includes Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi, Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanakha, Arun Govil as King Dashrath and Indira Krishnan as Queen Kaushalya. articles.title: Poison Ivy to get her own live-action series, ‘The Penguin’ showrunner Lauren LeFranc joins project
articles.summary: A television series centred on Poison Ivy, one of Batman's iconic villains, is in development at HBO with \"The Penguin\" showrunner Lauren LeFranc attached
articles.body: A television series centred on Poison Ivy, one of Batman's iconic villains, is in development at HBO with "The Penguin" showrunner Lauren LeFranc attached as a producer.The project would bring the green-haired DC Comics antagonist, known for her ability to control plants and manipulate people through seductive pheromones, into the spotlight in a live-action series, reported Variety.Poison Ivy has appeared in several live-action and animated adaptations of the Batman universe but has never headlined a film or television series.Uma Thurman famously portrayed the character in the 1997 film "Batman & Robin". The character has also featured in television shows such as "Gotham" and "Batwoman", and was voiced by Lake Bell in the animated series "Harley Quinn".LeFranc previously served as the showrunner of HBO's "The Penguin", the crime drama starring Colin Farrell as the Batman villain Oz Cobb.The series, which followed the events of Matt Reeves' 2022 film "The Batman", premiered in 2024 and received critical acclaim. Farrell won an Emmy and a Golden Globe for his performance.The potential Poison Ivy series comes as DC expands its slate of projects centred on its comic-book villains."Clayface", a horror thriller about another Batman antagonist, is part of the franchise's upcoming film slate, while HBO is also developing "The People vs. Gorilla Grodd", a comedic spinoff from James Gunn's "Superman".Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: John Anderson, country music hall of famer, dead at 71
articles.summary: John Anderson, inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame just last year, leaves behind 20 Top 10 hits and five No. 1 singles over decades.
articles.body: John Anderson, the Country Music Hall of Fame singer known for hits including "Swingin'," "Seminole Wind" and "Straight Tequila Night," has died. He was 71. Anderson died on Wednesday, Oct. 21. His death was announced by his family in a statement shared on his official Facebook page and acknowledged by the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. "It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend," the family wrote. "To the world, he was a gifted country music singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives. To us, he was so much more." The family described Anderson as "the heart of our family," and asked for prayers as they mourned his death. A cause of death has not been publicly announced. COUNTRY SINGER BRIAN 'NASHVILLE' DUCKWORTH, VOICE BEHIND FAMILY BAND TAYLOR MADE, DIES AT 56 Born Dec. 13, 1954, in Orlando, Florida, Anderson grew up in nearby Apopka before moving to Nashville after high school to pursue a career in country music. He signed with Warner Bros. Records in 1976. Anderson rose to prominence in the early 1980s with a traditional country sound influenced by artists including Merle Haggard and George Jones. His early hits included "I'm Just an Old Chunk of Coal" and "Wild and Blue," followed by "Swingin'," which earned him the Country Music Association's Single of the Year award in 1983. He also received the CMA Horizon Award that year. GEORGE STRAIT PULLS OFF INCREDIBLE CAREER ACCOMPLISHMENT WITH STUNNING CONCERT His traditional sound helped shape country music's New Traditionalist movement, which gained momentum in the 1980s. After a period of declining commercial success in the late 1980s, Anderson returned to the charts in the early 1990s with "Straight Tequila Night," "Seminole Wind" and "Money in the Bank." Over his career, Anderson recorded 20 Top 10 country hits, including five No. 1 singles, according to the Country Music Hall of Fame. He was inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2014 and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024. "John Anderson was a one-of-a-kind song stylist who proved that fresh innovations were best born from time-honored traditions," Kyle Young, CEO of the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum, said in a statement. Young praised Anderson's distinctive voice and his ability to draw inspiration from traditional country music. "He was already a diamond then, and a diamond he always will be," Young said, referencing Anderson's 1981 recording of Billy Joe Shaver's "I'm Just an Old Chunk of Coal (But I'm Gonna Be a Diamond Someday)." In their statement, Anderson's family said his impact extended far beyond his music. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "His music will live on, but for us, his greatest legacy will always be the love he gave his family and the memories we will carry with us forever."

articles.title: Rajinikanth’s ‘Jailer 2’ crosses Rs 549 crore worldwide in seven days, claims biggest first week in Tamil cinema history: ‘The record maker and the record breaker’
articles.summary: Rajinikanth’s ‘Jailer 2’ has registered a major box office milestone, with the makers announcing a worldwide collection of more than Rs 549 crore in its
articles.body: Rajinikanth’s ‘Jailer 2’ has registered a major box office milestone, with the makers announcing a worldwide collection of more than Rs 549 crore in its first seven days in theatres. Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, the action entertainer was released worldwide on October 15 and has delivered a strong opening-week performance, according to its production house, Sun Pictures.The makers have described the sequel’s first-week collection as the highest in Tamil cinema history. The announcement adds to the buzz around Rajinikanth’s latest outing as the film enters its second week in theatres.‘The record maker and the record breaker’: ‘Jailer 2’ crosses Rs 549 crore worldwideAnnouncing the film’s first-week achievement, Sun Pictures wrote, “The record maker and the record breaker! 549+ CRORES WORLDWIDE! The highest-grossing first week collections in Tamil cinema history! #Jailer2 Industry Mega Blockbuster.”The production house’s announcement puts ‘Jailer 2’ above the Rs 549 crore mark worldwide in its first seven days. Sun Pictures has also claimed that the film has recorded the biggest first-week collection in Tamil cinema history.The figure represents the makers’ official worldwide gross announcement; independent trade estimates may differ. The milestone nevertheless places the sequel’s opening-week performance firmly in the spotlight and gives the film a significant benchmark to build on during its ongoing theatrical run.‘Jailer 2’ box office run gets a boost from the festive periodReleased on October 15, ‘Jailer 2’ arrived in theatres during a period that included the weekend and Dussehra festivities. The holiday period offered audiences additional opportunities to catch the film, contributing to the atmosphere around its opening week.Rajinikanth leads the ensemble, which also features Ramya Krishnan, SJ Suryah, Vidya Balan and several other actors in key roles. Nelson Dilipkumar, who directed the first ‘Jailer’, returns to helm the sequel, while Anirudh Ravichander has composed the music.The combination of Rajinikanth’s screen presence, action sequences, comedy and an ensemble cast has helped the film attract attention across markets. Its performance in the coming days will determine how far it can extend its opening-week momentum.‘Jailer 2’ eyes more box office recordsWith Sun Pictures reporting more than Rs 549 crore worldwide in seven days, ‘Jailer 2’ now faces the challenge of sustaining its run through the second week and beyond. The first ‘Jailer’ reportedly collected around Rs 604 crore worldwide over its theatrical run, giving the sequel a prominent franchise benchmark to chase.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
